newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian c.bank cuts refinancing rate from Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: Russian c.bank cuts refinancing rate from Oct 21.

text.p: Russia's central bank is cutting its refinancing rate to 60 percent from 80 percent with effect from October 21, bank first deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told Reuters on Friday.
Aleksashenko also said that, from October 21, the bank would cut its Lombard credit rates by 10 percentage points.
The rate on seven-day Lombard credits would be cut to 20 percent from 30 percent, on 14-day credits to 40 percent from 50 percent and on 29-day credits to 50 percent from 60 percent.
Aleksashenko said the decisions were taken by the central bank board of directors on Friday.

He gave no reason for the rate cuts. When the refinancing rate was last lowered, to 80 percent from 110 percent on August 19, he said it was due to the low level of inflation and a fall in yields on government securities.
Consumer prices rose 31.7 percent in the year to September, down from a year-on-year rate of 37.1 percent in August.

The average yield on a new tranche of three-month Treasury bills fell to 42.17 percent at an auction on Wednesday from 54.69 percent on October 2 but the average yield on an issue of six-month bills rose to 56.00 percent from 49.63 percent.
The latest reduction takes the refinancing rate to its lowest since May 1992 when it was raised to 80 percent from 50 percent.

The central bank does not actually lend money at its refinancing rate but the rate gives an important signal to the economy and many contracts and central bank penalties for commercial banks are linked to it.
